title: Why Natural Latex Beats Memory Foam
imageAlt: Natural latex pillow compared with memory foam
description: Memory foam traps heat and reacts slowly. Here is why natural latex is the better choice for cool, supportive, restorative sleep.
body:
Memory foam traps heat and responds slowly. Natural latex springs back instantly, sleeps 3-4°C cooler, and is naturally antimicrobial. Here is why the switch matters for deep sleep.

The Heat Problem

Memory foam is petroleum-derived and traps body heat, raising skin temperature by 2-3°C during sleep. Natural latex has an open-cell pin-core structure that channels air continuously. In India's warm climate, this difference is critical.

Response Time

Natural latex rebounds in under 1 second. Memory foam takes 3-5 seconds, creating a sinkhole effect that misaligns your spine while it recovers. KRIT pillows use Dunlop-process latex that maintains consistent support all night.

The KRIT Difference

Every KRIT pillow uses 100% natural Hevea latex from GOLS-certified Karnataka estates. No synthetic blends, no chemical fillers. Just pure rubber tree latex, processed and certified.

title: How the Right Pillow Height Changes Everything
imageAlt: Choosing the right pillow height for your sleep position
description: Back, side or stomach sleeper? The right pillow height keeps your neck aligned and stops morning stiffness. Here is how to choose yours.
body:
The wrong pillow height is the single biggest cause of neck pain and poor sleep quality. Here is how to find yours.

Back Sleepers

Need a 2-3 inch pillow that supports the natural cervical curve without pushing the head forward. Our Half Pillow (2 inch) or Contour Pillow are ideal.

Side Sleepers

Need the most height — 3 inches — to fill the gap between shoulder and ear. The Half Pillow (3 inch) or Contour Pillow maintain neutral spine alignment.

Stomach Sleepers

Need the lowest possible profile, sometimes no pillow at all. Our Half Pillow (2 inch) works well, or the Soap Shape Pillow for gentle support.

title: The Sleep Environment: Temperature, Air & Your Bedroom
imageAlt: A calm bedroom set up for better sleep
description: Temperature, air quality and a calm bedroom matter as much as your pillow. Simple, science-backed changes for deeper sleep.
body:
Your bedroom environment affects sleep quality as much as your pillow and mattress. Here are the science-backed changes that work.

Temperature

The ideal sleep temperature is 18-20°C. Your body needs to drop its core temperature by 1-2°C to enter deep sleep. In Indian summers, this means AC at 20°C, not 16°C.

Air Quality

Dust mites in synthetic pillows trigger allergies that fragment sleep. Natural latex is naturally antimicrobial and dust-mite resistant — no chemical treatment needed. KRIT pillows are multi-washed and hypoallergenic.

Light

Even 10 lux of light suppresses melatonin production. Use blackout curtains or a sleep mask. Your phone screen at night delays sleep onset by 30-45 minutes.
